sources.label: Alaska prohibited and restricted noxious weeds
sources.caveat: List membership establishes statewide regulatory applicability only. It does not establish state or county occurrence, absence, or survey non-detection.

sources.label: Alabama administrative code noxious weeds
sources.authority: Alabama Department of Agriculture and Industries
sources.caveat: List membership establishes statewide regulatory applicability only. Incorporated federal lists require separate versioned acquisition. Misspellings and synonyms are never expanded without explicit review.

sources.label: Arkansas noxious weeds rule
sources.caveat: List membership establishes regulatory relevance for Arkansas certified-seed standards only. Genus rows and contextual rice rows require exact row-level review and do not imply occurrence.

sources.label: Arizona noxious weeds rule
sources.authority: Arizona Department of Agriculture and Arizona Secretary of State
sources.caveat: Official pages were human-readable but automated direct acquisition returned challenge pages on 2026-07-27. No applicability event may publish until a valid official artifact is retained and hashed.

sources.label: California noxious weed species regulation
sources.authority: California Department of Food and Agriculture
sources.caveat: California's designated current-code page was browser-serialized, retained, hashed, and reviewed on 2026-07-30. The page states currentness through July 17, 2026, Register 2026 No. 29. Exact catalog binomials establish California regulatory applicability only. Genus, synonym, hybrid, variety, aggregate, conditioned, and unmatched rows remain blocked.

sources.label: Colorado noxious weed rules
sources.authority: Colorado Department of Agriculture and Colorado Secretary of State
sources.caveat: The official Department of Agriculture page was browser-serialized, retained, hashed, and reviewed on 2026-07-30 because direct non-browser requests were blocked by the official site. Exact catalog binomials on Lists A, B, C, and Watch establish Colorado regulatory applicability only. Unmatched taxonomy remains blocked, and statewide distribution descriptions create no county claims.

sources.label: Connecticut prohibited invasive plants
sources.caveat: The official 2026 supplement was retained and hashed on 2026-07-30. Exact currently effective catalog binomials establish Connecticut regulatory applicability only. Unmatched taxonomy and restrictions effective in 2027, 2028, or 2030 remain explicitly blocked.

sources.label: Delaware invasive plant restrictions
sources.caveat: The current Delaware Department of Agriculture page and May 2026 final order were retained and hashed on 2026-07-30. Exact current invasive-list and watch-list catalog binomials establish Delaware regulatory applicability only. Future enforcement dates, unmatched taxonomy, and twelve named cultivar exemptions remain explicit context and do not create species-level not-applicability.

sources.label: District of Columbia invasive pollinator plants guide
sources.authority: District of Columbia Department of Energy and Environment
sources.caveat: The official DOEE page is an advisory purchase-and-removal guide, not a regulation. The official invasive table was retained through an analytics-free deterministic HTML serialization. Exact catalog binomials establish high-priority District applicability only. Genus rows, combined rows, source spellings, abbreviations, and unmatched taxonomy remain blocked. List silence creates no not-applicable, occurrence, absence, or survey claim.

sources.label: Florida noxious weed and invasive plant rule
sources.authority: Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
sources.caveat: The official final adopted Rule 5B-57.007 document, effective September 28, 2020 and presented as the latest final rule on August 1, 2026, was retained and hashed. Exact catalog binomials on the noxious and prohibited-aquatic lists establish Florida regulatory applicability only. Genus rows, unmatched taxonomy, named exceptions, and cultivar conditions remain blocked. Pending proposals remain separate from effective law, and no list row establishes county occurrence or negative evidence.

sources.label: Georgia noxious weed seed rule
sources.authority: Georgia Department of Agriculture and Georgia Secretary of State
sources.caveat: The current official Rule 40-12-4-.01 page was retained, hashed, and reviewed on August 1, 2026. Exact catalog binomials establish Georgia seed-commerce regulatory applicability only. Genus, composite, misspelled, variety, exception, and unmatched rows remain blocked. The incorporated 7 C.F.R. 360 list reuses the existing APHIS national artifact and was not reacquired. No row establishes county occurrence or negative evidence.

sources.label: Hawaii noxious weed rules
sources.caveat: The agency's current program page and FAQ identify Chapter 4-68 as the operative noxious-weed list and link a scanned 15-page rule copy. The exact current program-linked PDF was retained, hashed, extracted through an older text cross-check, and visually reviewed on August 1, 2026. Exact catalog binomials establish Hawaii regulatory applicability only. Genus, variety, synonym, source-spelling, and unmatched rows remain blocked. The adopted list's island free-or-relatively-free column creates no county occurrence, absence, not-detected, or not-applicable claim.

sources.label: Idaho noxious weeds rule
sources.caveat: Rule membership establishes statewide regulatory applicability only. EDRR membership may explicitly include taxa not known in Idaho, so it never establishes occurrence.

sources.label: Indiana terrestrial plant rule and noxious weeds
sources.caveat: List membership establishes statewide regulatory applicability only. It does not establish state or county occurrence, absence, or survey non-detection.

sources.label: Federal noxious weeds under 7 CFR 360.200
sources.authority: USDA Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service
sources.caveat: Federal list membership establishes regulated applicability in each explicit projected jurisdiction. It does not establish occurrence, county status, absence, non-detection, or not-applicability for unlisted taxa.
